title: Help-Free Dequeue-Tail Divergence
pattern: A lock-free queue dequeue operation that fails to "help" advance a lagging `tail` pointer when `head` and `tail` are found to be equal but the queue has elements.
why_bad: It violates the lock-free liveness invariant. If an enqueuer thread is suspended after updating `next` but before swinging `tail`, the queue becomes structurally inconsistent. Dequeuers will permanently spin or report an empty queue unless they actively help swing the lagging `tail` pointer.
detection: A lock-free queue implementation where the dequeue method does not contain a CAS operation to help advance the tail pointer when it lags.
counterexample: The standard Michael-Scott queue where dequeuers actively help advance the tail.
